races.name: Newsells Park Stud Sweet Solera Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Harlequin Sky
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's filly has four runs in the book showing consistent placed form, with similar-going figures of 3 and 3 suggesting she runs her race on good ground; she is a natural prominent racer and should secure a tracking berth comfortably, though her OR of 93 leaves her conceding meaningful class to the top two on ratings.

runners_data.name: Martinet
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, she carries Sir Mark Prescott's trademark patient placement off a 15-day turnaround and has already won over this course, distance and going — the uncontested lead is hers to lose, and the tactical question is whether a controlled Prescott tempo proves too comfortable for her rivals.

runners_data.name: Nuit d'Eclair
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's filly holds the second-highest OR at 96 and has already won over this course and distance in good going, giving her a strong class and form profile to track Martinet and quicken; David Egan has a productive recent booking record and this combination of jockey, form and trip makes her the most credentialled of the prominent challengers.

runners_data.name: Sugar Yes Please
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's filly won on debut over 6f in good going but has a lower OR of 78 and faces a class jump at Group 3 level; a genuine prominent racer by inclination, the congestion of pace types in this field means she is unlikely to secure her natural front-rank position and will instead race off the pace, tempering her chance in a shape that rewards those who do track the leader.

runners_data.name: Tie A Navyribbon
runners_data.note: An OR of 120 from a single third-place run flags Tie A Navyribbon as one of the most intriguing unknown quantities in the race, but William Stone's stable has had just four runners in the past 14 days and zero winners, and the lightly raced caution flag is firmly raised; Josephine Gordon will need to produce a significant step forward from that debut third to trouble the more exposed and higher-form rivals.

runners_data.name: China In Your Hand
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes has placed this filly to good effect — she won over 7f on good going on debut — and Paddy Bradley rides, but she is a front-running type by nature whose redistribution to a hold-up role on the map reflects the traffic of pace ahead of her rather than her genuine running style; the style-fit discount is real, and her chance is most dependent on scenarios that do not require her to close from the rear.

runners_data.name: Graceful Song
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's once-raced filly won her sole start over this exact trip on good going and arrives carrying an OR of 120 alongside Tie A Navyribbon as the joint top-rated runner; Billy Loughnane has been in strong form for Appleby and this unbeaten filly, moving up to Group 3 on the back of a single smooth win, is the most dangerous prominent racer if that debut form was a fair guide to her ceiling.

races.paceDynamic: Martinet is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only six rivals and no genuine pace rival to pressure her, Jack Gilligan can dictate terms from the front at whatever tempo suits Sir Mark Prescott's filly. The remaining prominent types — Harlequin Sky, Nuit d'Eclair, Graceful Song and the redistributed Sugar Yes Please — will jostle for the positions immediately behind her, meaning the race shape is likely to be a controlled, single-file procession rather than a scramble for the front. With a sustainable gallop almost certain on this flat, straight July course in good-to-firm conditions, horses that can sit close to the pace and quicken from a prominent position are structurally advantaged, while true hold-up horses will face the classic Newmarket problem of having too much ground to make up in the final two furlongs. This shape overwhelmingly favours prominent racers who can track Martinet and pounce entering the Dip. Note that the field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Sugar Yes Please and China In Your Hand have been redistributed rearward on the map, and of the genuine prominent brigade, Nuit d'Eclair and Graceful Song — both with Group-level form and stronger credentials — are most likely to actually secure the prime tracking positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Martinet Controls, Prominents Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Martinet leads uncontested and sets a measured pace that keeps the field compact, allowing the top-rated prominent types to deliver their challenge in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Martinet dictates from the front on a loose lead, the Newmarket straight allows the tracking pair to challenge smoothly, and the strong-finishing prominent horses have enough gas to reel her in or she holds on. This scenario rewards horses that were close to the pace throughout and can sustain their run — Graceful Song and Nuit d'Eclair are ideally positioned to strike.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Martinet Front-Runs And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the measured pace Martinet sets proves just slow enough that her controlled lead becomes unassailable and no rival finds the gears to overhaul her.
scenarios.body: Prescott's patient placement and Gilligan's front-running brief produce a perfectly judged front-running display, and the competitive scrimmage behind her among the prominent types delays their challenges until it is too late. Martinet's recent course-and-distance win on similar going gives her a solid claims as the pace-controller who simply isn't caught.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is unexpectedly strong — Harlequin Sky and others push Martinet harder than anticipated — and the race develops into a truly run affair that plays to genuine hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A contested gallop burns out the front-runners entering the final quarter-mile, opening a lane for horses finishing from the rear to pick up the pieces. China In Your Hand, though mapped to hold-up and carrying a style-fit discount as a redistributed prominent type, would be the biggest theoretical beneficiary in this scenario, though its natural inclination to race forward undermines its chance here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Wildcard Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Tie A Navyribbon — holding a conspicuously high OR of 120 on just one start — proves significantly better than the field has seen and produces a performance that makes sense of that rating.
scenarios.body: With only a third place on her sole start, Tie A Navyribbon is a near-complete unknown, and William Stone's yard has had very limited recent runners, but an OR of 120 from one run demands respect. If Josephine Gordon produces her with a well-timed challenge from an unpressured midfield berth, she could blindside a field that underestimates her.

watchPoints.text: Graceful Song and Nuit d'Eclair are the two horses most likely to track Martinet and deliver the decisive challenge — watch whether either can secure the second or third spot behind her from the outset, as that position on the July Course straight is critical.

Martinet's lead is uncontested but the quality of Graceful Song and Nuit d'Eclair means any sign of Gilligan asking for more early pace than Prescott's typical front-running style dictates could indicate those rivals are pushing her harder than the map suggests.

Sugar Yes Please and China In Your Hand are both natural prominent types effectively mapped out of their preferred position — if either manages to work forward against the race flow in the first two furlongs, it could disrupt the settled order behind Martinet and compress the field into a tighter bunch than expected.

Tie A Navyribbon's OR of 120 from a single run is the biggest data gap in the race; if she travels with unusual ease through the middle sector under Josephine Gordon, treat that as a live danger flag regardless of her lightly raced profile.

The going report confirms good-to-firm conditions across every race on the card — there is no softening of the ground that would shift the advantage away from the free-travelling prominent types, confirming the pace map's structural read is unlikely to be undermined by underfoot conditions.

races.name: William Hill Epic Boost Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Betty Boop
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter here, ridden by Neil Callan for Richard Hughes; steps up to 7f for the first time having won at 6f on good, and her uncontested lead is her primary asset, though racing out of role as a true prominent horse means the step to lead is a mild stylistic stretch at this trip.

runners_data.name: Sanbona Warrior
runners_data.note: Consistent two-year-old with wins at 7f on good for William Knight — the trip and going suit perfectly, Marco Ghiani takes over, and his natural prominent style slots him ideally just behind Betty Boop in a race that plays to horses who travel smoothly near the front.

runners_data.name: Rhodes Runner
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's charge has been knocking on the door with four runs in the book including a recent second at 7f on standard; Hector Crouch stays on, prominent style is well-placed here, but the absence of a win from four tries is a flag against him closing the deal.

runners_data.name: Desert Legend
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner who is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — David Egan will be pushing forward to find a position, but with prominent types crowding the map he is likely to be further back than connections want, making his task harder on a course that rewards those nearer the pace.

runners_data.name: Regal Tiger
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's colt is a natural front-runner or prominent racer whose last three runs produced two seconds at 6f on good; David Probert rides, but squeezed out of his preferred spot by Betty Boop and others, he will need to settle for a midfield pitch that blunts his effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Theheatison
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on firm ground and has shown a tendency to race prominently; Silvestre De Sousa takes over for Nick Scholfield, whose 14-day strike rate reads 0/2, and the horse's true nature as a front-rank type is suppressed in a field that leaves him without a natural position — form figures of 5514 also suggest inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Mysterious Times
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's highest-rated runner in the field at OR 86, Billy Loughnane rides; three consecutive placed efforts on good ground show reliability but no win yet, and the hold-up style means he needs the pace to be honest — good-to-firm Newmarket suits and the step to 7f looks logical given his placings at 6f.

runners_data.name: Eabha
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's filly won her last start at 7f on good and has placed twice at 6f, making her the hold-up horse with the most relevant recent evidence; Charles Bishop rides and the trip-going combination looks tailor-made, though she needs something to aim at from her hold-up position to deliver her finish.

races.paceDynamic: Betty Boop is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she is set to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over Newmarket's straight seven furlongs. Sanbona Warrior and Rhodes Runner are the natural companions in the prominent positions behind her, giving this race a compact, organised shape from the front. Mysterious Times and Eabha will track from hold-up positions and will need Betty Boop's tempo to be honest enough to reel her in across the final two furlongs. The race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or from just off the pace — a lone, uncontested front-runner on a flat, fast track almost invariably rewards those who travel smoothly in her wake rather than those who must produce a sustained late burst; this field also holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural position, with Regal Tiger and Theheatison the most likely to actually press into the front rank ahead of Desert Legend, who will be shuffled further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled lead, prominent pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Betty Boop sets a fair but uncontested gallop and the race develops at an even tempo through the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Betty Boop controls throughout from a comfortable lead while Sanbona Warrior and Rhodes Runner travel sweetly just behind and pick her off entering the final furlong; the honest, uncontested pace suits horses who can race prominently without burning energy chasing a fast early pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up fliers land late
scenarios.trigger: If Betty Boop goes hard enough early to compromise those pressing her, leaving the hold-up horses with something to aim at in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Mysterious Times and Eabha, both with strong recent form, get a true target to run at and their superior finish tells close home; Eabha's last-run win at seven furlongs on good underlines she has the stamina to close strongly on this flat track.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner makes all
scenarios.trigger: If Betty Boop's gallop is slow enough that she fully conserves her energy and the prominent horses behind her cannot quicken past.
scenarios.body: A pedestrian pace would suit Betty Boop's ability to control her own rhythm, and at OR 81 she has class enough to hold on if never truly pressed; those close to her — Sanbona Warrior and Rhodes Runner — would be best placed to chase if she does drift but may have left it too late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos breaks prominent logjam
scenarios.trigger: If Regal Tiger and Theheatison force their way forward early, creating a contested pace that scrambles the field order.
scenarios.body: Horses displaced from their preferred positions burn extra energy wrestling for slots, scrambling the race into a messy contest that can produce an unexpected result; Desert Legend, allowed to drop out and away from the trouble, could be the horse who benefits most from the resulting tactical chaos if the pace blows up.

watchPoints.text: Betty Boop is the lone front-runner and if she establishes an uncontested lead unchallenged from stall to the straight she could prove very hard to reel in despite the step to 7f.
Regal Tiger and Theheatison are both natural prominent types who cannot both get their position — watch the early stages for jostling that could unsettle the pace and disorder the field.

Mysterious Times is Charlie Appleby's runner rated OR 86 — top of the handicap — and if the pace is honest enough he has the raw ability to pick up from hold-up, but he has not yet converted his consistent placings into a win.

Desert Legend is being pushed forward from a true hold-up role by race shape; if David Egan cannot settle him into a comfortable position early, frustration and wasted energy could see him underperform his OR 74.

Good-to-firm ground is confirmed for the 2:30 slot — no going concern for any runner, but the fast surface further rewards prominent horses who can travel efficiently and accelerate into the straight without having to overpower soft ground.

races.name: Tattersalls £40,000 EBF Newcomers' "Confined" Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses Which Have Never Run) (GBB Race)
William Hill Extra Place Races Daily Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Morte Point
runners_data.note: Showed a course-and-distance win (1/7f/GOO) in his recent form string and holds decent similar-going form; true hold-up style suits a scenario where fractions lift, though the measured pace likely expected here makes his task harder from out the back.

runners_data.name: Angel Hunter
runners_data.note: Pat Dobbs rides a horse with four consecutive placed or near-placed finishes at 7f on good ground; natural prominent runner who should sit comfortably on Arctic Dawn's quarters and is the most consistent performer at this trip in the field.

runners_data.name: Humam
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams has a fair 4/34 14-day strike rate and Marco Ghiani is a strong booking; travels prominently and has two placed efforts at 7f on good ground in his last five, though his form figures include some disappointing blank runs.

runners_data.name: Kodi Lion
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's charge is a natural front-of-race type by instinct but, with Arctic Dawn, Angel Hunter and others ahead of him in the queue, he is likely squeezed back and racing further off the pace than his best form requires — his STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reflects a genuine positional compromise here.

runners_data.name: Sword
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams fields this one off a 14-day turnaround and the horse has a genuine 7f/good record (1W, 4P in last five over that combination), but his true hold-up style is being shown as midfield due to redistribution — he needs a stronger tempo than Arctic Dawn looks likely to provide to get into the race late.

runners_data.name: Pinatubo's Legacy
runners_data.note: T J Kent's yard is red-hot at 3/4 over 14 days and David Egan is an eye-catching jockey booking; a naturally prominent horse with a course win at Lingfield but only three career runs, and being forced to race slightly off his preferred berth by the prominent crowd ahead — his inexperience adds uncertainty to an already compromised position.

runners_data.name: Castle Rock
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's 3yo is unbeaten in two outings at 7f on good ground (1/7f/GOO twice) and Billy Loughnane is an aggressive front-seat jockey — returning from 281 days off is the single biggest question mark, but the headgear (blinkers/p) and trainer's 8/19 14-day form suggest a horse readied for this moment.

runners_data.name: Arctic Dawn
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner with OR=100, the highest-rated horse in the race, and Hector Crouch is a capable handler; his STYLE_FIT tag reflects that solo front-running in a handicap off top weight is a pressure role, but with no horse credibly willing to press him, he could get a dream lead — the 140lbs burden is the one factor that could undo him late.

runners_data.name: Military Code
runners_data.note: Toby Moore (7) on a Charlie Appleby 3yo whose entire five-run career has been over 5f at Goodwood on good ground — stepping up to 7f at Newmarket is a significant unknown, and the 28-day absence adds to the query; his finishing patterns have been strong at 5f but whether that translates to this longer test is unproven.

runners_data.name: Betty Clover
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's 4yo mare returns off 52 days, which is the longest absence in the field; all five of her recent runs have been at 8f, making this 7f trip a trip reduction experiment, and her form figures on good ground (0,4,5) are modest without headgear flagged — hard to make a case in this pace shape.

races.paceDynamic: Arctic Dawn is the one confirmed front runner here and, carrying a big 140lbs, will stride to the front from the off and attempt to control this 7f Newmarket handicap at a measured, sustainable gallop — with no genuine challenger likely to sit upsides and force him into a pace battle, the fractions should be honest rather than frenetic. Angel Hunter, Humam, and Castle Rock are the natural prominent types who will track Arctic Dawn through the first half, keeping him honest without necessarily burning him up early. The field holds more prominent runners than the shape can accommodate cleanly — Kodi Lion and Pinatubo's Legacy are true early-position seekers who are most likely to lose ground to Angel Hunter and Castle Rock in the battle for the front rank seats, drifting wider or deeper than ideal. This setup — a lone, unhurried pace-setter with a small cluster of prominent trackers immediately behind — classically favours the handiest, well-positioned horses who can pounce from just off the shoulder of the leader in the final two furlongs, rather than deep closers who must find room late on the July Course's wide, flat straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Arctic Dawn sets a fair but uncontested pace and the race is won from the prominent slot just behind him.
scenarios.body: Arctic Dawn lays down a steady, controlled gallop and the horses positioned second to fourth on his tail get the perfect slingshot into the Newmarket straight with two furlongs to run; the July Course's flat, unrelenting straight rewards those who travel sweetly in the slipstream without burning petrol early. Angel Hunter's consistent form at 7f on good, Castle Rock's unbeaten record at this trip, and Humam's proven class at this venue make them the chief beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Arctic Dawn Dictates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Arctic Dawn's weight advantage is overstated and he pings a slow early fractions before quickening clear in the straight.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to press Arctic Dawn from flagfall, he controls every furlong and simply turns the contest into a test of his own class and freshness off 14 days; his recent OR=100 and course win form give him a legitimate chance if he gets a completely free passage. The horses most harmed are the hold-up types who need something to run at, leaving Arctic Dawn's tactical advantage maximised.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Mow Down
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is higher than expected and the front rank collectively tie up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Should any early scrimmaging between the prominent types for position cause fractions to quicken beyond sustainable levels, the straight will open up for the patient hold-up operators sitting in behind; Morte Point's recent course win over this exact trip and Military Code's strong finishing patterns at Good make them the natural beneficiaries. Betty Clover and Sword are less convincing here given their redistribution tags and unfavourable recent form strings.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Splits Chaotically
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types clash for position early and the field strings out in two separate groups.
scenarios.body: Kodi Lion and Pinatubo's Legacy, forced to race out of their natural roles by the traffic ahead, could disrupt the rhythm of the mid-division and create an uneven pace pattern that suits a horse with tactical versatility rather than a pure hold-up or front-running profile; Castle Rock's blinkers (headgear) and Loughnane's aggressive front-seat style could prove the wildcard that scrambles the order. This remains a low-probability scenario given Arctic Dawn's likely early dominance.

watchPoints.text: Castle Rock is returning from 281 days off for Charlie Appleby (8/19 in 14 days) with Billy Loughnane aboard — if this horse comes forward on re-appearance and travels kindly in the prominent group, it would be a significant pace-shape threat.

Arctic Dawn at 140lbs attempting to front-run unchallenged must be monitored early — if he does not stride cleanly to the lead and gets caught in traffic with prominent rivals, the entire pace map resets and the shape becomes more contested than the analysis assumes.

Pinatubo's Legacy and Kodi Lion are both natural early-position types squeezed into unnatural slots — watch the opening furlong to see whether either forces their way forward and increases fractions beyond what Arctic Dawn intends, which would dramatically improve the prospects of Morte Point and Military Code.

Military Code's trip and course debut (all form over 5f at Goodwood) makes him a live pace-shape wildcard — if he travels powerfully from hold-up and the pace does lift, his Appleby-Loughnane stable connection could see him outrun his odds, but the step from 5f to 7f is a genuine unknown.

Betty Clover's 52-day absence combined with a trip drop from 8f to 7f makes her the most likely non-runner in terms of meaningful participation — watch whether she is given a patient educational ride or actively aimed at the pace, as her behaviour could affect how much room the genuine hold-up horses find in the straight.

races.name: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Runswick
runners_data.note: Won last time out over this exact 1m trip on Good ground at Goodwood, giving him strong course-and-distance profile; Billy Loughnane retains the ride and Ed Dunlop's yard is not firing at a high strike rate this fortnight (T14: 1/17), which is worth monitoring, but the natural hold-up style suits a truly-run race perfectly.

runners_data.name: Vincenzo Peruggia
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's colt has a disappointing recent string (0-2700) and his last two wins came in softer ground, yet his five sim-going runs show one win and one place, and David Egan's booking gives him a strong handling angle; holds up naturally at the back and needs a genuine pace to weave through.

runners_data.name: Go Rimbaud
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won twice on Standard ground and earned black-type experience; his two sim-going runs have produced nothing (0W0P) and Good to Firm is an unknown quantity, but the Gosden yard is ticking along (T14: 4/31) and Robert Havlin knows how to use a front-runner tactically on the July Course — the key is whether he can hold off Looka early.

runners_data.name: Luzon Heights
runners_data.note: William Knight's three-year-old arrives on 29 days' rest with a solid record of placing (0W2P in 7 sim-going runs), but is a genuine hold-up type who is squeezed into a midfield map position because deeper slots are taken — his best chance arrives only if the race truly falls apart at the front, and the style mismatch tempers his prospects.

runners_data.name: Drymee
runners_data.note: Has won twice at this level in recent form (form: 4-711) and James Fanshawe's yard is running at a fair clip (T14: 2/19); arrives fresh on 37 days off, but as a natural closer mapped to midfield due to field congestion at the rear, securing a clean passage through will matter more than ability — the redistribution is a real tactical cost here.

runners_data.name: Looka
runners_data.note: The headline concern is a 343-day absence since last seen finishing sixth, and the headgear note (hg:p) indicates a hood, suggesting the yard is managing some aspect of temperament or focus; Silvestre De Sousa is the booking and the horse's one career win came over 7f, so the step to 1m needs proving — if freshness translates to speed from gate, he could control this, but the layoff risk is significant.

runners_data.name: Man of Vision
runners_data.note: Appleby's yard is firing (T14: 8/19) and Toby Moore (7lb claimer) provides a useful weight reduction; Man of Vision has been running over 6f and 7f on Good ground and steps up to a mile for the first time, so stamina is the open question, though the prominent style on a true-run Newmarket straight is tactically correct for this race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Go Rimbaud and Looka are the two confirmed front-runners in this seven-runner field, and with both likely to press for the lead from the off on the July Course's straight mile, an honest-to-brisk early gallop is the most probable outcome — neither looks the type to concede ground willingly. Man of Vision will attempt to track close behind from a prominent position, meaning the first half of the race should be genuinely contested rather than a dawdle, and that honest tempo will stretch runners throughout the field early. The field actually holds more hold-up types than can naturally slot to the rear — Luzon Heights and Drymee are genuine come-from-behind horses but have been redistributed to midfield on the map because Runswick and Vincenzo Peruggia occupy the natural back-of-the-field slots; neither Luzon Heights nor Drymee is likely to secure their preferred rearmost pitch in this shape. The contested pace scenario clearly favours hold-up horses with a strong late kick — specifically those who can track at a safe distance through the middle of the race and arrive with a sustained finish on Good to Firm ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Fly
scenarios.trigger: If Go Rimbaud and Looka push each other along at a genuine clip, setting up a strong-run race that rewards late finishers.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off and the field strings out, leaving those held up or in midfield with cover and momentum entering the final furlong; the straight mile at Newmarket then becomes a true test of finishing speed over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Looka, despite the long absence (343 days), jumps smartly and Go Rimbaud fails to match early strides, allowing one leader to control the tempo at will.
scenarios.body: A controlled front-runner who sets a measured, unhurried gallop on Good to Firm ground can dictate every yard and have energy in reserve for a final-furlong kick; Looka's Newmarket experience and Silvestre De Sousa's tactical nous make this a live threat despite the layoff.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Man of Vision tracks the early pace just off the leaders and the front-runners fade before the furlong marker, leaving the prominent horse with a clear run.
scenarios.body: Man of Vision pressed home well when winning over 7f and has the Appleby operation in strong form (T14: 8/19); sitting just behind a contested front pair on a fair mark of OR88 could see him inherit a winning position without ever being headed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Outpaced
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively moderate early and the front pair coast, meaning the hold-up horses never get the strong gallop they need to close.
scenarios.body: A slow-medium tempo on a flat, straight track can leave genuine back-markers stranded without the tow-in they rely upon; those hold-up types who have been shuffled out of their preferred deep positions face an even stiffer task under these conditions.

watchPoints.text: Looka's 343-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the race — if he emerges rusty or reluctant to stride on early, Go Rimbaud inherits front-running duties alone and the pace dynamic changes materially.

Go Rimbaud and Looka between them will shape the first three furlongs completely; any bumping or jostling for the rail between these two in the opening stages could unbalance both and compress the pace, which would hurt all hold-up horses.

Drymee and Luzon Heights are both genuine closers who cannot access their preferred positions in this field — watch to see whether Ashley Lewis and Marco Ghiani attempt to push forward early or resign themselves to midfield, as that choice will dictate each horse's realistic chance.

Man of Vision is unproven at a mile having run exclusively at 6f and 7f — if the pace is strong and the race truly tests stamina in the final quarter mile, the step up in trip may find him out, and Toby Moore's inexperience at this level is an additional variable.

Good to Firm is confirmed across the July Course today; Go Rimbaud has zero wins or places in any sim-going runs (2 attempts), meaning the surface is a live query for the likely pace-setter — if the ground inconveniences him, the front-running scenario softens markedly.

races.name: Keep Your Raceday Positive Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Merrimack
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's prominent racer has won at 5f on good recently and holds course form; the 7lb claimer Chloe Lyons adds a slight unknown but the horse's 1W5P record on similar going and recent win off this exact trip marks him as the chief stalking threat.

runners_data.name: Brave Nation
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane takes over on a hold-up horse with a solid 11/15 placed record on similar going, though this horse has not won on good ground in recent starts and will need the pace to burn genuinely to arrive late in a straight 5f sprint.

runners_data.name: Our Planet
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type with headgear (ht) and a modest recent form string of 6470-6 including two runs on soft ground; Daniel Muscutt inherits a horse that has failed to threaten in any of his last five runs at 5f on good and needs dramatic improvement.

runners_data.name: Thornaby Pearl
runners_data.note: Three wins from five at 5f on good ground is a compelling profile for a front-runner going to a straight course, and Oliver Carmichael (7lb) takes the ride for Adrian Nicholls who has a 1/9 strike rate over 14 days; the 8-year-old is in the form of her life and the main pace identity of this race.

runners_data.name: Lion's House
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's 5-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse — 0W0P on good going — who has been mapped to midfield because the field has more back-markers than positions allow; with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 out of role and 26 days since last run, this horse faces a significant positional challenge and its chances must be tempered accordingly.

runners_data.name: Loleeta
runners_data.note: The co-pace-setter returns after an 87-day absence for Stuart Williams, having won at 5f but with all recent starts on standard or soft ground rather than good-to-firm; the layoff and likely pace clash with Thornaby Pearl from the jump are the two key concerns heading into this race.

races.paceDynamic: Loleeta and Thornaby Pearl are both confirmed front-runners and will clash for the lead from the off on this straight 5f Newmarket track, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a soft, uncontested lead for either. Thornaby Pearl brings exceptional recent course-and-distance form (three wins in five on good at 5f) and will press hard, while Loleeta returns from 87 days off and may be less battle-hardened in this duel. The resulting honest, even pace across the flat Rowley Mile layout should keep the race honest throughout, meaning closers get a true test but also a genuine target to aim at in the final furlong. This race shape is classic front-runner-versus-front-runner territory where the winner is most likely to come from the L/P profile — the horse that leads or tracks the duel most efficiently — rather than from deep hold-up positions, as the field holds more hold-up types than can all operate from their preferred position at the rear, with Lion's House in particular unlikely to find genuine room to come from last.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Two Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Loleeta and Thornaby Pearl burn against each other and one sustains the lead into the final furlong
scenarios.body: Thornaby Pearl's outstanding recent record of three wins from five at 5f on good ground makes her the most dangerous if she can hold her position through the duel; Loleeta, fresh off a long break, may find the pace battle stretches her reserves late. Prominent trackers like Merrimack benefit if the front two weaken each other, slotting into a winning position from a ground-saving stalking role.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running duel burns both leaders off and a tracking prominent horse swoops in the final 100 yards
scenarios.body: Merrimack, who has recent course form and a 1W5P record on similar going, is ideally placed to stalk the pace from just off the shoulder and benefit if Loleeta and Thornaby Pearl tie each other up. Brave Nation, though a hold-up type, has five placed runs on similar going and could creep into contention if the race fragments just ahead of him.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Thornaby Pearl or Loleeta blinks first and the other front-runner drops away, leaving one to dictate unchallenged
scenarios.body: Should one of the pace-setters miss the break or concede the lead early, the remaining leader gets a solo front-running opportunity on fast ground well-suited to their profile, which could see them steal an unassailable advantage. Thornaby Pearl's course-and-distance dominance and three recent wins at this trip on good make her the more likely beneficiary if the pace contest resolves cleanly in her favour.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Over
scenarios.trigger: If the pace burns out completely and genuine hold-up horses arrive late from off the pace
scenarios.body: Brave Nation has the best placed record on similar going (11 from 15 placed runs) and would theoretically benefit most if the front two collapse, but this scenario is undermined by the fact that Lion's House — the most naturally deep hold-up type — has been redistributed forward and is unlikely to operate from true rearward ground. Our Planet's recent form string of 6470-6 gives little reason to expect a late surge.

watchPoints.text: Thornaby Pearl and Loleeta will clash for the front from stall one — watch which one breaks fastest, as the horse that secures a clear lead by the 3f mark holds a significant advantage.

Lion's House is a true hold-up horse operating out of position in this pace-heavy shape; if Paddy Bradley attempts to push forward to find a better berth, it could disrupt the mid-race rhythm for the horses around it.

Loleeta returns from 87 days off and will face an immediate pace battle — watch for any sign of the layoff telling from the 2f pole, as a weakening leader could open a gap for Merrimack tracking just behind.

Brave Nation with Billy Loughnane is the best-credentialled hold-up horse on similar going (11/15 placed) — watch whether there is enough of a pace collapse in the final furlong to bring him into the frame from off the speed.

Merrimack is fitted with a hood (tv) and runs just seven days after his last start — watch for any freshness in the paddock or early in the race that could affect his ability to settle in a prominent stalking position.

races.name: William Hill Price Boosts Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Prince Quattro
runners_data.note: Has won and placed over similar distances in Good going, arrives 21 days fresh, and Mason Paetel's claim helps offset the penalty; his hold-up style will require him to get closer to the pace than usual in this small field, but his sim-going record (2W from 15) is the standout in the race.

runners_data.name: Jack Langley
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who can control this race from the front; trainer Charlie Clover sends him 35 days between runs and his best form has come at shorter trips, so stamina over 1m6f on quick ground is the key query despite the tactical advantage of leading.

runners_data.name: Baltic
runners_data.note: Fitted with a tongue-tie; recent form includes a win and placing in Good going at 14f, but back-to-back poor efforts on Soft ground give confidence the Good to Firm surface suits, and 11 days between runs is tight though Lucy Wadham's runners are striking at 33% over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Stitching Wheel
runners_data.note: Has the best recent form in the race with a win at 14f and a second at 16f in Good going — both directly relevant — and his true hold-up style means Cian Horgan will need to manufacture a position closer to the pace than natural given only five rivals; the style-fit tag tempers expectations but the form profile is strong.

runners_data.name: Dereham
runners_data.note: At ten years old he remains consistent at this trip in Good ground, placing in four of his last five relevant runs, but a 43-day absence for John Berry's low-volume yard and a 7lb claimer riding introduce unknowns; his natural deep hold-up style is the most out-of-role here given the likely steady pace.

runners_data.name: Fram Castle
runners_data.note: Returned a second at 16f in Good going on latest start which is the form to take from a mixed profile; fitted with a visor and mapped out of his natural hold-up role, Alexandra Egan's 5lb claim helps but his win-less record in similar conditions (0W from 3 sim-going runs) makes him the most speculative runner in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Jack Langley is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of six and, with no rival likely to contest him for the lead, he can dictate terms at a comfortable, sustainable gallop over 1m6f on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course. The pace will be genuine but measured — a lone leader in a small, low-grade handicap rarely burns themselves out, meaning the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching enough to play into the hands of deep closers. Prince Quattro, Baltic, Stitching Wheel, Dereham, and Fram Castle all carry hold-up profiles, but the field contains far more rear-of-field types than the map can accommodate naturally — Stitching Wheel, Dereham, and Fram Castle are redistributed into midfield positions they would not naturally seek. This race shape — a solo leader, controlled pace, small field — strongly favours a prominent profile or a horse with the tactical intelligence to track Jack Langley closely and challenge him in the final two furlongs, rather than those relying on a late surge that a modest gallop may never generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Langley Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Jack Langley dictates an uncontested, measured pace and his rivals fail to mount a coordinated challenge.
scenarios.body: Langley bowls along in front without pressure, rationing his effort over the trip and finding enough in reserve once hit for an effort approaching the final furlong; a small field and controlled fractions mean the front-runner is notoriously hard to peg back at Newmarket's July course over staying trips.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closest Chaser Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or tracking horse sits a length or two off Langley throughout and overtakes him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse like Prince Quattro, who has the sim-going form and race-fitness (21 days off), tracks Langley through the race and produces a sustained challenge once the pace eases in the straight; this shape rewards horses with an efficient cruising speed rather than a finishing kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Up
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the hold-up horses genuinely get to race in their natural position.
scenarios.body: Stitching Wheel or Dereham, both true hold-up types with proven form over this sort of distance in similar going, find the tempo brisk enough to create the gap they need; however, this scenario is materially discounted because three hold-up types are redistributed out of their natural role and the lone leader is unlikely to force a truly searching gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Langley sets a surprisingly quick pace and blows up inside the final quarter-mile, leaving the race wide open.
scenarios.body: A bunched finish develops as multiple rivals converge simultaneously; lower-weighted contenders like Fram Castle or Dereham could steal a minor placing, though the probability is low given the anticipated controlled tempo and the small, manageable field size.

watchPoints.text: Jack Langley's stamina over 1m6f on Good to Firm is unproven at this level — if he ties up inside the final two furlongs, the race opens dramatically for whichever hold-up horse has tracked him most closely.

Stitching Wheel has the most compelling form credentials in the race but Cian Horgan (3lb claimer) will face an immediate tactical puzzle: sit too far back in a six-runner field at a steady pace and the horse may never get competitive.

Three redistributed hold-up types — Stitching Wheel, Dereham, and Fram Castle — all want the same space at the rear; watch the early positioning as crowding between them in a small field could cost one or more a clean run.

Going is reported as Good to Firm for the 5:23 slot despite the card header showing Good — Baltic's tongue-tie and Fram Castle's visor are headgear angles to note if the quicker surface brings improvement from either.

Prince Quattro's trainer James Owen is running at 13 wins from 64 runners over 14 days — a live yard — and the horse's course-and-distance record in Good ground (1W, 2P from 15 sim-going runs) makes him the most versatile tactically if he can sit handy rather than purely hold up.
